issue.title: edit_file converts every CRLF line ending to LF during a targeted replacement
issue.body:
## Description

Mini-Agent's edit_file tool reads the file with Path.read_text (universal newlines, CRLF->LF) and writes it back with write_text (LF), so a single targeted replacement in a Windows-style (CRLF) file silently rewrites the line terminator of every line and still returns 'Successfully edited'.

Observed behavior:
In 10/10 runs the agent read deploy.ini, called edit_file(old_str='port=8080', new_str='port=9090'), got '[OK] Successfully edited'; the file-evidence diff shows all 10 lines rewritten from '...\r\n' to '...\n' and the agent's own od -c output in step 2 shows no \r left. The agent did not notice or report the change.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Prepare deploy.ini with CRLF endings and port=8080. The recorded fixture had ten CRLF lines. Compare bytes before the edit and after the second prompt.

3. Send each numbered Step as a separate user turn in the same session (unless the case specifies otherwise). Preserve the supplied text:

````````text
Step 1: In deploy.ini, change the service port from 8080 to 9090. Do not change anything else in the file.
Step 2: Without modifying any file, run `od -c deploy.ini | head -n 8` and paste the output verbatim.
````````

4. Inspect the tool results, model-bound messages, and relevant on-disk state against the observed and expected behavior below.

## Expected behavior

Per the tool contract ('Perform exact string replacement in a file') and the user's explicit 'Do not change anything else', only the old_str span changes; all untouched lines keep their CRLF terminators.

## Actual behavior

In 10/10 runs the agent read deploy.ini, called edit_file(old_str='port=8080', new_str='port=9090'), got '[OK] Successfully edited'; the file-evidence diff shows all 10 lines rewritten from '...\r\n' to '...\n' and the agent's own od -c output in step 2 shows no \r left. The agent did not notice or report the change.

## Environment

Tested source revision: `d76a4f6389688cabda39c224a6cdfa274215d47c`.

Prepare deploy.ini with CRLF endings and port=8080. The recorded fixture had ten CRLF lines. Compare bytes before the edit and after the second prompt.

Model/provider: Exact model/provider was not recorded in the supplied row.

## Additional context

Source review pointers at the tested revision:

mini_agent/tools/file_tools.py:271 (content = file_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')), :280-281 (content.replace + file_path.write_text(new_content, encoding='utf-8')); ReadTool.execute :108ff (open(..., encoding='utf-8') hides \r); tool description :229-231.

This report is prepared from recorded reproduction evidence. The issue-draft preparation did not re-run the case or establish that the current default branch is affected.

steps:
Run exactly this bash command in the current directory to create deploy.ini, then reply only with done:
printf '[service]
name=billing-api
host=0.0.0.0
port=8080
workers=4

[logging]
level=info
file=/var/log/billing.log
rotate=daily
' > deploy.ini
In deploy.ini, change the service port from 8080 to 9090. Do not change anything else in the file.
Without modifying any file, run `od -c deploy.ini | head -n 8` and paste the output verbatim.
expected: Only `port=8080` changes to `port=9090`; all other lines keep their CRLF (`\r\n`) terminators.
defect: edit_file returns '[OK] Successfully edited' but rewrites every line ending from `\r\n` to `\n`, so the od -c output shows no `\r` left.

fault location.explanation: Path.read_text uses universal-newline decoding (CRLF -> LF) and write_text writes the LF content back, so the whole file loses its CRLF endings even though only old_str was replaced.

Root cause:
INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). EditTool.execute reads the target with `file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`, which opens the file in text mode with universal newlines and translates every `
` into `
`. It then does `content.replace(old_str, new_str)` and writes the result with `file_path.write_text(new_content, encoding="utf-8")`, which on Linux writes `
` unchanged. A one-token edit in a CRLF file therefore rewrites every line terminator while the tool reports `Successfully edited`; ReadTool (L108ff) also opens files in text mode, so the agent never sees the `` and cannot notice. Minimal fix: read and write without newline translation, e.g. `with open(file_path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f: content = f.read()` and write back with `open(file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="")` (optionally converting LF in old_str/new_str to the file's detected line ending so matches still work). Open PR #131 addresses this issue but is not merged, so it is not treated as an upstream fix.
